title: Montezuma Cypress: Ancient Ahuehuetes You Can Visit
meta_description: The species holds the fattest trunk on earth, in Oaxaca. Four Montezuma cypresses mapped in Florence, Lisbon, Madrid and Naples.
intro: This is the species that holds the fattest trunk on earth, the Arbol del Tule in Oaxaca, and the four mapped here are working in the same direction if nowhere near the same scale. Florence's is seven metres around and was hit by lightning barely a decade ago. Lisbon's, in the Jardim da Parada, is six and a half metres around and the biggest thing in a garden that fills an entire city block. Taxodium mucronatum is Mexico's national tree, the ahuehuete, planted at springs by the Aztecs, and Naples has nicknamed its own the Tree of Thule after the giant in Oaxaca. Madrid's, in the Retiro's parterre, comes with two origin stories that cannot both be true and estimates running from 200 years to 390. In a mild winter it keeps enough of its needles never to look properly bare.
